motions.motion_text:
The draft budget was tabled at the Council meeting of November 8, 2023. The Emergency Preparedness and Protective Services Committee report on the draft budget will be considered by Council at its meeting of December 6, 2023.
Councillor M. Luloff declared an interest on this item (3. B. i. of the Committee’s Roadmap Motion - Ottawa Fire Service Operating Resource Requirement  - Communications - page 7 of the Committee’s Full Budget Book), as his spouse is employed by a software firm that provides services to Ottawa Fire Services and would receive funding from, or would potentially receive funding from, these budget line items.  He recused himself and did not participate in the vote on this particular Budget line item during Committee’s consideration of the Roadmap Motion.
At the outset, Mr. Kim Ayotte, General Manager, Emergency and Protective Services (EPS) Department, introduced the following, who were present to speak to a detailed slide presentation overview of the Committee’s portion of the 2024 City of Ottawa budget (held on file with the Office of the City Clerk), and/or to respond to questions from Committee:
Vice Chair Hill read out the Committee’s ‘Roadmap’ Motion prior to the receipt of public delegations:
Motion NO EPPSC 2023-08-01
Moved by Vice-Chair Hill:
That the Emergency Preparedness and Protective Services Committee recommend that Council, sitting as Committee of the Whole, approve the Emergency Preparedness and Protective Services Committee 2024 Draft Operating and Capital Budgets as follows:
Committee then heard from the following public delegations:
[     + Slide presentations / visuals / videos held on file with the Office of the City Clerk. ]
Ms. Vania Karam, Chair, Accessibility Advisory Committee, had earlier registered to speak to Committee, but was unavailable.
Following questions to the delgations and to staff, and with Committee discussions having concluded, the Roadmap Motion was put before Committee and was ‘CARRIED’, as presented, with Councillor M. Luloff recusing himself from the vote on line item 3. B. i. - Ottawa Fire Service Operating Resource Requirement  - Communications (page 7 of the Committee’s Full Budget Book) prior to the vote on that particular line item.
The following Direction to Staff was also given, with staff agreeing to take the Direction:
Direction to staff (Councillor L. Dudas):
That staff return to Committee, by April 2024, with an FTE analysis / update pertaining to staffing resources required to address work pressures related to the Vacant Property By-law, in advance of Committee and Council’s consideration of the 2025 Budget.

sub_agendas_items.title: City of Ottawa Spay/Neuter Clinic

attachments.attachment_title: EPPSC Inquiry 2023-06 - S Devine - City Spay-Neuter Clinic.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Submitted by Councillor S. Devine (Inquiry EPPSC 2023-06)
The HolliBell Foundation is a registered not-for-profit (in the process of obtaining charitable status) whose mission is to promote animal welfare through funding the spaying and neutering of domestic, feral and stray animals, which helps both the community as a whole and individual residents. Similar to the City’s Spay/Neuter Clinic, the objective of sterilizing these animals is to control population growth and reduce the number of unwanted animals in need of shelter and care. The Foundation is currently using the facilities of a spay neuter clinic in Brockville.
As the city of Ottawa’s Spay & Neuter Clinic is currently open for surgeries only 4 days per week, the Foundation has expressed interest to the City in accessing its Spay/Neuter Clinic facilities during the days it is not currently operational in order to expand its animal sterilization efforts in the Ottawa area.
Recently, the Hollibell Foundation and other individuals and residents have made inquiries about whether Ottawa’s Spay & Neuter Clinic can be made available for the other 2 – 3 days per week when the clinic is not operational, should another licensed veterinarian and/or credible organazations have the capacity to deliver professional services, and assuming the additional costs could be covered by other parties.
Recognizing that there may legislative barriers in this regard and that the current Spay/Neuter Clinic’s own veterinarian is operating at capacity, could staff review the feasibility and costs of expanding the current Clinic facilities and operation to other parties in order accommodate additional surgeries at a time when issues of animal control is a growing concern.
